message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year in 2003.

He entered the NBA directly from high school, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers in the 2003 draft. LeBron quickly became a dominant force in the league, earning the NBA Rookie of the Year award in 2004 and multiple MVP honors. He has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (two stints), the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers, winning championships with each team:

- **2007** – Cleveland Cavaliers (first NBA title for the franchise)
- **2012 & 2013** – Miami Heat
- **2020** – Los Angeles Lakers

Beyond his on‑court achievements—four NBA MVP awards, 19 All‑Star selections, and numerous scoring, rebounding, and assist records—LeBron is also known for his philanthropy, notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise School” in Akron to support at‑risk children. He has also pursued a career in entertainment, producing films and television shows, and is an outspoken advocate on social justice issues.
